copies.headline: Isaac's Questionable Tags Won't Save Him Twice
copies.body:
Adam wins this at every position and wins it worse in the margins. Jayden Daniels in a 40.5-total home game against Philly isn't a ceiling play, but Adam doesn't need one with Jaxon Smith-Njigba against Chicago and a Walker/Irving backfield that both sit in competitive games Tampa and Kansas City are favored in by a field goal or less. Isaac's problem isn't his top line — Javonte Williams in a 54.5-point Dallas game is the single juiciest spot on either roster — it's that his top line is held together with injury tags. Ja'Marr Chase questionable, Saquon questionable, Meyers questionable, Kincaid questionable, Skattebo questionable.
Behind those names Isaac has Ryan Flournoy and Kalif Raymond, which is not a receiving corps so much as a waiver-wire alibi. Adam's at 144.0 a game with an 81% all-play; Isaac is 11th in scoring and plus-0.7 wins on luck, meaning 3-4 flatters him. Isaac leads the head-to-head 5-3, which is the only thing he's winning here.

copies.headline: Logan Scores Plenty, Loses Anyway, Again
copies.body:
Logan has the better quarterback and the better single-game ceiling — Burrow against a Titans team getting ten points in a 46.5 is the cleanest spot on either roster — but the edges stop there. His running back room is six names and five question marks: Warren is the only healthy piece, and Pittsburgh-Cleveland has a 39.5 total, the lowest on the board. Love, Charbonnet, Allen and Allgeier are all tagged, meaning Logan might be starting whoever gets cleared Sunday morning. Tight end is Parkinson at nine, also questionable, with Isaiah Likely at zero behind him.
Grant's receiver group carries it. Flowers in Baltimore-Buffalo, total 54.5, with the Ravens chasing points late, is the best game environment anyone owns here. St. Brown's tag matters, but Watson at 14 in a 47.5 softens it, and Goedert or Strange both give him ten at tight end. Logan's 44-33 all-play says he deserves better. He won't get it.

copies.headline: Christian's Bad Luck Meets CJ's Thin Receivers
copies.body:
Christian is 2-5 with the third-best scoring average in the league and a 46-31 all-play, which is the statistical definition of getting mugged every Sunday. The edges here are quarterback and receiver. Trevor Lawrence gets Indianapolis in a game Jacksonville is favored by 10, and CeeDee Lamb headlines a Cowboys-Cardinals total of 54.5 — the highest number on the board — with Brandon Aubrey attached to the same scoreboard. CJ counters with Michael Penix Jr. as a 2.5-point road underdog in a 44.5-point game, which is fine, not scary.
CJ's problem is receiver depth that depends on tags. Emeka Egbuka and Rashee Rice are both questionable, Alec Pierce is on IR, and Parker Washington is the top projection on a team playing from 10 points behind. The backfield is genuinely even — Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard and Ollie Gordon II against Chase Brown and Bhayshul Tuten — so running backs won't save it. If Rice and Egbuka sit, CJ is starting DK Metcalf and prayers.

copies.headline: Leif's Injury Report Is a Receiving Corps
copies.body:
Leif has Josh Allen in a 54.5 shootout with Baltimore and Derrick Henry on the other sideline, which is a terrific way to start and a terrible way to finish. After that it's Stefon Diggs (questionable) at 13, Omar Cooper Jr. at 10 and Chris Godwin at 9 — and nothing behind them, because Davante Adams is on IR, Marvin Harrison Jr. projects at zero and Mike Evans is a question mark. McCaffrey and Montgomery both carry tags with no real RB2 insurance beyond Kimani Vidal's eight. That's a top-heavy roster held together by two names.
Kaleb's 109.2 per game is ninth in the league and his all-play is 44 percent, so none of this is earned. But the depth is real: Drake London in a 44.5 game Atlanta likely trails, Tre Tucker and Ladd McConkey, Carnell Tate chasing points as a 10-point dog in Cincinnati. Even if Breece Hall sits, Jeanty and Harvey cover it. Leif wins QB by eight and loses RB and WR by fifteen combined.

copies.headline: Two 1-6 Teams, One Unavoidable Winner
copies.body:
The positional math says Mitchell, barely: 37 to 32 at running back, a dead heat at receiver and tight end. The problem is how much of that is held together with tape. Jahmyr Gibbs is questionable and carries 25 of Mitchell's projected points by himself; behind him sit Rachaad White in a 40.5-total Washington game and Jordan Mason. Matthew Golden, DJ Moore and Tyler Warren are all tagged too, and the fallback is Nico Collins and Christian Kirk at zero and Travis Kelce at nine. Four coin flips in one lineup isn't depth, it's a prayer.
Noah's edge is that his best stuff is clean. Drake Maye is a seven-point favorite in Miami with Rhamondre Stevenson and Hunter Henry stacked behind him, and James Cook sits in a 54.5-total Bills-Ravens game that should keep scoring into the fourth. Garrett Wilson gets Las Vegas. Noah is the worse team by all-play — 24-53, last in the league — but he's scored 107-plus three straight weeks while Mitchell has posted 85.5 and 79.4. Floor beats fragility here.

copies.headline: Peter's 5-2 Is A Costume, John's Isn't
copies.body:
The projections say Peter wins three of four positional groups, and almost none of it is safe. Lamar Jackson is questionable in a 54.5-point game at Buffalo — he's the single biggest swing on the board either way, and behind him sits Justin Herbert at 11. A.J. Brown and George Pickens carry the same tag, and Brown is in a 43.5-total Dolphins game where a touchdown-favored Patriots team would happily grind the second half. Peter's edges are real on paper and conditional in practice; Bijan Robinson in a 44.5-total road underdog spot isn't rescuing anyone.
John's advantages are structural. Trey McBride at 18 with Brock Bowers as the fallback is a seven-point tight end gap that doesn't require anything to break right. The Rams stack of Puka Nacua, Kyren Williams and Matthew Stafford as 6.5-point home favorites is clean, and John has scored 128.4 a game to Peter's 111.6 with a 65 percent all-play to Peter's 43. Peter is two wins luckier than he's earned. Older brothers tend to collect.

intro: The tightest game on the board is Leif at Kaleb, where Kaleb holds a narrow edge in a matchup that decides which 5-2 team gets to keep breathing down Adam's neck — and Peter, the third team at 5-2, has the misfortune of drawing a John roster that's healthier at the skill spots. The clearest gap is Christian over CJ, which is its own kind of insult: a 2-5 team walking into a 4-3 team's week and being the one with the better starting lineup. Mitchell and Noah are also playing football this week, technically, with Noah favored in the only game where the loser arguably comes out ahead.
